title: Taint is not carried across delegate_to_agent, so a tainted orchestrator turn can trigger unconfirmed server-side writes through a sub-persona
evidence: aura_backend/aura_core/tools/delegation.py:84-96 (tool is not side_effecting; policy.py:136-139 never holds it in a tainted context)
aura_backend/aura_core/kernel/kernel.py:399-426 (taint derived only from the child's own retrieval/caller_context/resume)
aura_backend/aura_core/tools/records.py:10-14 (create_*/update_*/delete_* run with no confirmation when untainted)
aura_backend/aura_core/container.py:1400-1403 (CRUD tools registered whenever personal_os_store is wired)
current_behavior: A parent turn tainted by a quarantined chunk, fetch_url output or caller context may still call delegate_to_agent (policy_ok). The child turn starts untainted, so a planned create_task/delete_finance_record etc. in the child executes immediately. The tool's own refusal (delegation.py:152-158) only fires for sub-turns that report needs_confirmation, which untainted CRUD calls never do.
expected_behavior: ADR-006: a turn whose context was quarantined cannot run a side-effecting tool without confirmation, across any number of kernel hops.
recommendation: Add an inherited-taint input to TurnRequest, set it from context.tainted in delegate_to_agent and OR it into the child's taint at kernel.py:426/734; add a tests/unit/test_delegation.py case asserting a tainted parent makes the child's side-effecting call return confirmation_required.
confidence: High (code); Med (practical exploitability requires the planner model to follow injected text and a persona holding CRUD tools)

title: write_files is registered for the engineer capability but absent from the engineer persona's grant, so the persona can never use it
evidence: aura_backend/aura_core/agents/registry.py:213-225 (grant lists write_file and edit_file, not write_files, and no mcp_* name)
aura_backend/tests/architecture/test_workspace_local_tools.py:34 and tests/unit/test_engineer_tools.py:149-210 exercise the tool with a hand-built ToolContext, bypassing the persona grant
current_behavior: The D6 atomic multi-file write (and every MCP-bridged tool) is unreachable from the engineer persona; only an engineer_agent-capable caller using the unrestricted orchestrator persona can reach them.
expected_behavior: Every tool built for the engineer is in the engineer's grant, pinned by a test comparing the grant against the registered engineer tool names.
recommendation: Add write_files (and a policy for mcp_* names) to the grant at registry.py:213-225; add a test asserting the grant covers build_sandbox_tools()+build_github_tools() names.

title: Engineer tooling is reachable under the orchestrator persona without the engineer prompt or multi-pass loop
current_behavior: A caller holding engineer_agent who leaves agent=orchestrator is offered run_command, git_push, github_commit_files etc. under the generic orchestrator prompt (no treat-output-as-data instruction) with max_plan_iterations=1. Tool-level policy still applies, so this is a prompt/UX gap rather than privilege escalation.
expected_behavior: A persona gate described as a second layer should constrain which prompt and loop the engineer tools run under, or be documented as tool-level only.
recommendation: Give orchestrator an explicit allowed_tools excluding required_capability tools, or correct the registry.py:226-232 comment.

title: _READ_TOOLS grants remember_fact (a durable write) to every persona, including decision_agent described as read-only
current_behavior: Every persona can write long-term memory into its scope without confirmation when untainted.
expected_behavior: A grant named _READ_TOOLS contains only reads; a persona documented as read-only cannot write.
recommendation: Move remember_fact out of _READ_TOOLS and grant it only to personas that should persist facts; fix the comment.
